reviews.body:
### 🟢 Approval recommended No active review issues are recorded for the fix to Kaspersky YARA rule parsing. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR Fixes Kaspersky YARA parsing when a line begins with a closing brace followed by another rule’s header, preventing malformed indicator patterns and lost rules. **Changes:** - Separates the closing brace and recognized rule header before splitting rules. - Adds parametrized regression tests for LF and CRLF line endings and plain, `private`, and `global` headers. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `external-import/​kaspersky/​tests/​tests_connector/​test_yara.py` | Tests rule recovery across line endings and header variants. | | `external-import/​kaspersky/​src/​kaspersky/​utils/​yara.py` | Separates joined closing braces and rule headers for the existing splitter. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body:
**nit (non-blocking):** the split brace is re-emitted as `line[0] + "
"`, so on a CRLF feed the first rule ends in `}
` while its other lines end in `
`. The issue says the feed already has mixed endings, so this is probably harmless. If you want it byte-faithful, keep the original terminator, for example by taking it from the tail of `line`. The new test calls `.rstrip()` before comparing, so it wouldn't notice the difference.

**question (non-blocking):** the split only fires when a line starts with `}` and a rule header follows. A mid-line boundary (`... true }rule b {`) or a glued `}import "x"` would still not split. Does the feed produce either form? The rejected pattern in #7980 looks like the line-start form. `}import` can't matter for Master YARA, which uses `imports_at_top=True`. If you have a feed sample with a mid-line boundary, a regex split over the whole text would cover it. If not, this PR already fixes the reported case.

**suggestion (non-blocking):** the test covers only the positive path. Could you add a negative case that `}rule_b {` is not split, since `rule_b` doesn't start with `rule `? That would protect the `startswith(_RULE_STARTS)` guard. A case with three consecutive glued rules (`}rule b {` then `}rule c {` on separate lines) would also protect the `while` loop.

Done in 2d8f916: the re-emitted brace now keeps the original line terminator, and the test compares the end of the first rule exactly (no more `.rstrip()`).


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

I don't have a feed sample showing a mid-line boundary; the only form I know of is the line-start one from #7980. So I left the split limited to that case rather than running a regex over the whole text.


This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Added both in 2d8f916: `}rule_b {` is not split, and three rules glued on consecutive boundaries are all recovered. While doing this I noticed the `while` could never run twice (the remainder always starts with a rule header, never `}`), so it is now a plain `if`.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
